rv.q: But Prowse's production seems more concerned with effects than ideas.

This dark thought isn’t helped by the fact that, as played by the radiant Kara Tointon, Eliza may look a peach, but she doesn’t sound convincing either as an authentic cockney or as a trainee duchess – so Higgins clearly isn’t much of a voice coach either.

Their big showdown, played facing each other while seated on the red banquettes that are endemic to Prowse’s “theatrical” setting of red swags, false prosceniums and mottled pillars, is as electrifying as any version of that scene I can recall.
